course.title: AI-Powered DevOps Automation with n8n
course.subtitle: Build the deployment notifications, Kubernetes alerts, incident workflows and daily reports DevOps teams rely on with n8n and Mattermost, then add AI summaries a human reviews.
course.description:
A deployment fails at 3 a.m. A pod keeps crashing. Someone asks, again, what shipped yesterday. Every DevOps team answers the same questions by hand, every day.

This course hands that work to **n8n**. It watches your systems, posts one clear message to your team's **Mattermost** channel and, with **AI**, drafts the summary of a failed deployment before anyone opens the log. You build every piece yourself, live, and keep the result.

## What you'll build
- **Your own automation stack:** n8n and Mattermost with Docker Compose, on your laptop or on an AWS VM created with Terraform.
- **Deployment notifications:** your CI pipeline posts green or red to the team in seconds, behind a secret token. A GitHub Actions example is included.
- **Kubernetes alerts people trust:** crash loops, failed image pulls and pods stuck in Pending, one message per problem instead of a flood.
- **An incident workflow:** severity, escalation when nobody answers, acknowledgement and a resolved message.
- **A morning report:** yesterday's deployments, failures and service status, posted before your day starts.
- **AI summaries, done safely:** OpenAI reads a redacted log and drafts what failed, the likely cause and what to check. A person reviews it and makes the call.
- **A production setup:** PostgreSQL, queue mode with workers, backups, a pinned upgrade and a tested rollback.

## Why this course
- **Every lesson runs live.** You watch each workflow built, broken and fixed on a real system, not described on slides.
- **A ready-made lab for every hands-on lesson.** Compose files, scripts and workflows to import, with a step-by-step README, plus a short quiz with the answers explained.
- **Self-hosted and portable.** Everything runs on your own Docker host, and the Kubernetes workflows work on minikube, EKS and AKS.
- **AI with guardrails.** Secrets are removed before anything is sent, every answer is labelled as a draft with its token cost, and the AI never changes anything on its own.

## Who it's for
DevOps engineers, SREs and developers who are at home in a terminal and Docker and want their team to stop chasing the same information by hand. You don't need any n8n experience: you start from zero.
objectives: Deploy n8n and Mattermost with Docker Compose, locally or on an AWS EC2 VM built with Terraform, and keep their data safe
Build, test and publish n8n workflows with triggers, nodes, expressions and the Executions log
Send green and red deployment notifications from a CI pipeline through a token-protected webhook
Make workflows fail safely with retries, fallback paths, an error workflow and node-by-node debugging
Alert on Kubernetes crash loops, failed image pulls and pending pods with one message per problem
Turn repeated alerts into one incident with severity, escalation, acknowledgement and resolution
Schedule a daily report that gathers deployments, failures and service status into one message
Apply proven patterns: sub-workflows, signed webhooks, idempotency, rate limits, pagination and loop guards
Run n8n in production with PostgreSQL, queue mode, a protected encryption key, backups, upgrades and rollback
Use AI to summarise failed deployments, errors and incidents, with redaction, prompt-injection defences, cost tracking and human review
requirements: Comfortable with a terminal and basic Docker commands
Docker with the Compose plugin, and about 4 GB of free memory
Kubernetes lesson: minikube and kubectl (the lab explains both), or your own EKS or AKS cluster
AI lesson: your own OpenAI API key with a monthly budget limit
Optional cloud lesson: an AWS account, the AWS CLI and Terraform 1.5 or newer

lessons.title: Welcome: what you'll build in this course
lessons.summary: What the course covers and who it's for: the self-hosted n8n and Mattermost stack, the automations you'll build, how AI summaries fit with a human in charge, and how the labs and the four modules work.

lessons.title: How n8n and Mattermost work together for DevOps
lessons.summary: See how the two fit together: an event triggers a workflow, n8n does the work and your team reads the result in a channel. One everyday example, the real screens, and why teams self-host both.

lessons.title: Deploy n8n and Mattermost with Docker Compose
lessons.summary: Deploy n8n, Mattermost and a demo website from one Compose file. Read it block by block, fix a real port conflict, log in to both apps and prove your data survives new containers.

lessons.title: Set up Mattermost channels and incoming webhooks
lessons.summary: Create a team, an alerts channel and its incoming webhook, keep the webhook URL out of your workflows, and prove that n8n can post to the channel from inside Docker.

lessons.title: Tour n8n and build your first workflows
lessons.summary: Learn n8n from zero: a full tour of the editor and settings, then two workflows that post real messages to Mattermost. Run them, publish them, fix a real error and catch a real outage.

lessons.title: Run the lab on an AWS VM with Terraform
lessons.summary: Move the same lab to an AWS EC2 VM so schedules and webhooks keep running when your laptop sleeps. Terraform creates it, an SSH tunnel reaches it, and terraform destroy removes every resource.

lessons.title: n8n vocabulary: workflows, triggers, nodes and executions
lessons.summary: The words you'll use every day in n8n: workflow, trigger, node, item, expression, execution and publish. Each one explained with an everyday example, an animation and the real n8n screen.

lessons.title: Send deployment notifications from your CI pipeline
lessons.summary: Your pipeline calls an n8n webhook after each deployment and the team sees a green or red message in seconds. Secure it with a token so forged calls get a 401, and wire it into GitHub Actions.

lessons.title: Send GitHub pull request updates to your team chat
lessons.summary: Turn every pull request event (opened, updated, reviewed, approved, merged, closed) from a real GitHub repository into a clear Mattermost message. Verify GitHub's signature, relay deliveries to a local n8n, and check the ping before you rely on it.

lessons.title: Handle failures with retries, fallbacks and debugging
lessons.summary: Break an API on purpose and make your workflows survive it: retries for short blips, a fallback path, an error workflow that alerts the team, and debugging a failed run node by node.

lessons.title: Automation and ChatOps vocabulary
lessons.summary: Webhooks or polling, cron, sub-workflows, idempotency, rate limits, queue mode and slash commands, explained with one café example, then shown where you meet each in n8n and Mattermost.

lessons.title: Alert on Kubernetes problems without the noise
lessons.summary: n8n checks a namespace every 30 seconds with a read-only service account and posts one alert per crash loop, failed image pull or pending pod. Break a real cluster three ways, then add a daily health report.

lessons.title: Manage incidents: severity, escalation and resolution
lessons.summary: Turn a flood of repeated alerts into one incident with a severity. Escalate when nobody acknowledges, show who is on it, and close the loop with a resolved message, on a real outage.

lessons.title: Schedule a morning report for your team
lessons.summary: Answer the team's morning questions automatically: a scheduled workflow collects deployments, failures and service status, writes one short report and posts it to Mattermost every day.

lessons.title: Advanced patterns: signed webhooks, idempotency and more
lessons.summary: Patterns for workflows that hold up: sub-workflows, signed webhooks, idempotency, rate limits and batches, pagination, loop guards, workflows in git and where the logs are. Each one tested live.

lessons.title: Run n8n in production: Postgres, workers, backups, upgrades
lessons.summary: Run n8n itself for the long term: PostgreSQL, queue mode with Redis and workers, the encryption key, backups and restores, a pinned upgrade with a rollback, and a disaster recovery drill.

lessons.title: Add AI summaries to your workflows, safely
lessons.summary: Let AI draft what failed, the likely cause and what to check. Redact secrets first, defend against prompt injection, label every answer as a draft with its token cost, and keep a human in charge.

lessons.title: AI incident triage: ranked hypotheses a human confirms
lessons.summary: A bad deploy triggers an alert; n8n gathers the deploy history and logs, and an AI model drafts three ranked hypotheses with exact evidence lines. The on-call engineer checks them, rejects a wrong guess, confirms the cause and rolls back.

lessons.title: Build an AI ops agent in n8n with tools, memory and guardrails
lessons.summary: Ask "why is payments slow?" and let an n8n AI Agent check health, metrics, logs and the runbook with read-only tools. Risky actions become requests: a separate approval workflow restarts only after a human clicks.

lessons.title: AI in CI/CD: explain a failed pipeline and suggest the fix
lessons.summary: When a GitHub Actions job fails, n8n reads the failed log, an AI model explains it in plain words and suggests a fix, and the team sees the draft in Mattermost. The AI explains and suggests; it never merges or deploys.

lessons.title: Continue your learning journey: AI for DevOps on AWS and Azure
lessons.summary: You can automate your team's work with n8n. The AI for DevOps masterclasses show you how to build the AI systems behind it, on AWS or Azure.
lessons.articleMd:
You can now run n8n in production and use it to watch your systems, manage incidents, report every morning and add AI that drafts while people decide.

If you want to build the AI side yourself, models, RAG, agents and MCP servers on a real cloud, the two **AI for DevOps masterclasses** are the next step. Each starts with the AI foundations and goes hands-on from there.

## AI for DevOps on AWS: From Fundamentals to Production
Amazon Bedrock chatbots and Knowledge Bases, AI agents that fix 502s, crash loops and Kubernetes workloads with your approval, your first MCP server, and AI in production on AWS.

[See the AWS masterclass]({{course:ai-for-devops-aws}})

## AI for DevOps on Azure: From Fundamentals to Production
Microsoft Foundry models and chat apps, RAG with Azure AI Search and Terraform, the same troubleshooting agents and MCP skills, and AI in production on Azure.

[See the Azure masterclass]({{course:ai-for-devops-azure}})
